title: A survey on the impacts of recommender systems on users, items, and human-AI ecosystems

bias_targets.methodology: Synthesizing empirical studies, sock-puppet audits, and agent-based simulations to evaluate the algorithmic amplification of partisan content, echo chambers, filter bubbles, and ideological polarization across social media platforms.

Reviewing empirical A/B tests and simulation studies that use metrics like the Gini index and average item popularity to measure 'concentration'—the disproportionate amplification of engagement toward already popular items, users, or mainstream content.

Reviewing observational studies of platform data (e.g., measuring revenue disparities between Black and White Airbnb hosts) and generative AI simulations that evaluate representation shifts using demographic prompts.

Aggregating controlled user studies and prompt-based evaluations that measure how generative AI models homogenize text toward Western-centric stylistic norms and assess their misalignment with cross-national cultural values.

Reviewing observational studies on demographic homophily in urban mapping platforms and generative AI simulations that evaluate representational distortion over iterative training using gender-specific prompts.
Reviewing generative AI simulation studies that use age-specific demographic prompts in iterative image-to-image synthesis to observe representation changes and model collapse.
